claims.statement: Refused surrender to Beinai and vowed to fight to the death.
Urged Shizu to remember Puyangwen and his wife before attacking Talan.
Offered himself as hostage in place of the women of Muzong’s household.
Warned Muzong’s dissenting kinsmen that he would not remain silent if they quarreled.

claims.action: Huandu was of the Wanyan tribe.
claims.sourceText: 歡都，完顏部人。

claims.action: His grandfather Shilu was Zhaozu's contemporary, clansman, and namesake; the two became fast friends and swore an oath: "In life we shall share one river's bank; in death one valley's grave."
claims.sourceText: 祖石魯，與昭祖同時同部同名，交相得，誓曰：「生則同川居，死則同穀葬。」

claims.action: The people called Zhaozu "Brave Shilu" and Shilu "Virtuous Shilu."
claims.sourceText: 土人呼昭祖為勇石魯，呼石魯為賢石魯。

claims.action: Zhaozu and Shilu plotted to recover them, went together beyond the ridge, and shot arrows tipped with burning tinder.
claims.sourceText: 昭祖與石魯謀取之，遂偕至嶺右，炷火於箭端而射。

claims.action: Zhaozu and Shilu then marched in force, seized their goods, and carried off the two women.
claims.sourceText: 昭祖及石魯以眾至，攻取其貲產，虜二女子以歸。

claims.action: Zhaozu took one for himself and Virtuous Shilu the other; each made his a concubine.
claims.sourceText: 昭祖納其一，賢石魯納其一，皆以為妾。

claims.action: The tribes still refused law and custom. Zhaozu showed his strength at Qingling and White Mountain and pressed into Subin and Yelan, with Virtuous Shilu at his side throughout.
claims.sourceText: 是時，諸部不肯用條教，昭祖耀武於青嶺、白山，入于蘇濱、耶懶之地，賢石魯佐之也。

claims.action: In Jingzu's day Shilu's son Hesun brought his tribe in submission and settled south of Hukai Mountain on the headwaters of the Anchu River.
claims.sourceText: 至景祖時，石魯之子劾孫舉部來歸，居於安出虎水源胡凱山南。

claims.action: Huandu was Hesun's son.
claims.sourceText: 歡都，劾孫子。

claims.action: When Shizu first came to power, Huandu inherited the post of military governor.
claims.sourceText: 世祖初，襲節度使。

claims.action: Huandu came in to counsel and went out to command on the field; he never left Shizu's side.
claims.sourceText: 歡都入與謀議，出臨戰陣，未嘗去左右。

claims.action: Beinai of the Wole clan had lived with his brothers north of the Anchu River since Jingzu's day. When Wuchun rebelled, Beinai was ready to join him and secretly won over the Woluguan water-folk, intending to destroy Huandu first.
claims.sourceText: 斡勒部人杯乃，自景祖時與其兄弟俱居安出虎水之北，及烏春作難，杯乃將與烏春合，間誘斡魯紺出水居人與之相結，欲先除去歡都。

claims.action: When his house burned, he secretly suborned the bondservant Bugesou to claim that Huandu and Hutu had set the blaze, and sent Zhudu to Shizu with the message: "Bugesou reports that the fire the other day was the work of Huandu and his party.
claims.sourceText: 會其家被火，陰約隸人不歌束，詭稱放火乃歡都、胡土二人，使注都來謂世祖曰：「不歌束來告曰'前日之火，歡都等縱之'。

claims.action: Huandu buckled on armor, seized his halberd, and rose. "He is a rebel. If they demand the Grand Preceptor's brothers, will you surrender them as well?
claims.sourceText: 歡都被甲執戟而起曰：「彼為亂之人也，若取太師兄弟，則亦與之乎。

claims.action: If they demand us, we will never go. If it must come to war, we shall fight to the last man."
claims.sourceText: 今取我輩，我輩決不可往，若必用戰，當盡力致死。」

claims.action: Muzong said: "How bold Huandu is! In my judgment he is entirely right."
claims.sourceText: 穆宗曰：「壯哉歡都，以我所見，正如此爾。」

claims.action: He gave Huandu a horse and said: "When you fight, ride this one."
claims.sourceText: 贈歡都以馬，曰：「戰則乘此。」

claims.action: Shizu then went to Beinai and, standing across the Biecih River, said: "Bugesou has named Huandu and the rest as the arsonists. I shall keep our agreement to the letter.
claims.sourceText: 世祖乃往見杯乃，隔鱉刺水而與之言曰：「不歌束既告縱火由歡都等，謹當如約。

claims.action: It later came out that the fire had been set by Beinai's servant Achuhushan. Beinai had sought a pretext for strife and had framed Huandu.
claims.sourceText: 既而聞之，放火者杯乃家人阿出胡山也，杯乃欲開此釁，故以誣歡都雲。

claims.action: Dusk had fallen and Shizu had barely fifty or sixty riders. Huandu plunged into the enemy line and fought back and forth four times over before Shizu, wounded, called a halt.
claims.sourceText: 日已曛，惟從五六十騎，歡都入敵陣鏖擊之，左右出入者數四，世祖中創乃止。

claims.action: The tribal chiefs Saola and Fuzhe Talan watched to see which side would win and withheld their support. Both had previously joined Lapei and Machan, so Shizu meant to destroy them on the march home and spurred his horse forward.
claims.sourceText: 於是騷臘勃堇、富者撻懶歡勝負不助軍，而騷臘、撻懶先曾與臘醅、麻產合，世祖欲因軍還而遂滅之，馳馬前進。

claims.action: Talan was Empress Zhenhui's younger brother.
claims.sourceText: 撻懶者，貞惠皇后之弟也。

claims.action: Huandu dismounted, seized the bridle, and pleaded: "Have you no thought for your beloved younger brother Puyangwen and his wife?"
claims.sourceText: 歡都下馬執轡而諫曰：「獨不念愛弟蒲陽溫與弟婦乎。」

claims.action: Shizu was moved and drew rein.
claims.sourceText: 世祖感其言，遂止。

claims.action: Puyangwen is the Jurchen name for "younger brother" in Chinese.
claims.sourceText: 蒲陽溫者，漢語雲幼弟也。

claims.action: Of Shizu's maternal brothers Muzong was the youngest, and so earned that name.
claims.sourceText: 世祖母弟中穆宗最少，故雲然。

claims.action: Muzong remembered Huandu's counsel and later arranged for Talan's daughter Heluoshen to marry Huandu's son Gushen.
claims.sourceText: 穆宗德歡都言，後以撻懶女曷羅哂妻其子谷神。

claims.action: When Taizu pursued Machan, Huandu struck him in the head with an arrow and took him prisoner.
claims.sourceText: 太祖追麻產，歡都射中其首，遂獲之。

claims.action: Liao appointed Muzong, Taizu, Cibushi, and Huandu each to the office of xiangwen.
claims.sourceText: 遼人命穆宗、太祖、辭不失、歡都俱為詳穩。

claims.action: Woshan and Wotuo brought the Guli contingent in submission, and Shizu sent the tribal chief Xiebo to settle them.
claims.sourceText: 斡善、斡脫以姑裏甸兵來歸，使斜缽勃堇撫定之。

claims.action: Gushi, Bashi, and others of the Pucha tribe lured the troops into a city and trapped more than three hundred men.
claims.sourceText: 蒲察部故石、拔石等，誘其眾入城，陷三百餘人。

claims.action: Huandu was made commander-in-chief and sent to investigate Xiebo's loss of the force. He relieved Xiebo of his entire command, crushed Wuchun and Womouhan at Xiedui, and captured Gushi and Bashi.
claims.sourceText: 歡都為都統，往治斜缽失軍之狀，盡解斜缽所將軍、大破烏春、窩謀罕於斜堆，擒故石、拔石。

claims.action: When Cibushi stormed the stronghold of Wuchun and Womouhan he took Sanbin and Sada and their mother as well. He made her a secondary consort and raised the two boys.
claims.sourceText: 辭不失破烏春窩謀罕城，獲三濱、撒達，並獲其母，以為次室，撫其二子。

claims.action: While Muzong was out hunting at dawn, he rallied seven or eight armed men, forced their way into the palace, seized the inner gate, and took Empress Zhenhui and the household hostage.
claims.sourceText: 因穆宗晨出獵，糾率七八人操兵入宅，奪據寢門，劫貞惠皇后及家人等。

claims.action: Huandu went in to Azu'a and said: "What end do you intend for this plot of yours?
claims.sourceText: 歡都入見阿注阿曰：「汝輩所謀之事奈何。

claims.action: The women of the inner quarters are poor hostages; you only terrify them to no purpose.
claims.sourceText: 閨門眷屬豈足劫質，徒使之驚恐耳。

claims.action: You know me well. Take me instead."
claims.sourceText: 汝固識我，盍以我為質也。」

claims.action: He pressed the point again and again until Azu'a agreed. The empress was freed and Huandu held in her place.
claims.sourceText: 再三言之，阿注阿從之，貞惠皇后乃得解，而質歡都。

claims.action: They bound Huandu together with Alutaiwan, Alutaibuwan, and five others, linking their robe-hems, and marched with Azu'a. At the Liao border they set Huandu free.
claims.sourceText: 遂執歡都及阿魯太彎、阿魯不太彎等七人，以衣裾相結，與阿注阿俱行，至遼境，乃釋歡都。

claims.action: Huandu reached Jizhou, which was in fact Huanglong Prefecture, and sent riders by relay to cut off Azu'a's party, sparing only his kin.
claims.sourceText: 歡都至濟州，實黃龍府，使人馳驛要遮阿注阿黨屬，惟縱其親人使去。

claims.action: He then killed Sanbin and his mother, reported the whole affair to Liao, and asked that Azu'a be returned. Liao banished him to Yijin.
claims.sourceText: 遂殺三濱並其母，具報於遼，乞還阿注阿，遼人流之曷堇城。

claims.action: Later, homesick for his own country, Azu'a fled back and joined the registered Jurchen. He raided the dwellings of their officials, was seized, refused to yield, and was executed.
claims.sourceText: 其後，阿注阿懷思鄉土，亡歸，附於系案女直，因亂其官僚之室，捕之，不伏，乃見殺。

claims.action: Early in Muzong's reign, his cousins Xilie and Xiebo, together with his elder brothers, murmured dissent: "Those men made themselves lord and minister—what of us?"
claims.sourceText: 穆宗襲位之初，諸父之子習烈、斜缽及諸兄有異言，曰：「君相之位，皆渠輩為之，奈何？」

claims.action: Huandu said: "If you quarrel among yourselves, I shall not stand idly by."
claims.sourceText: 歡都曰：「汝輩若紛爭，則吾必不默默但已。」

claims.action: At his words the company fell quiet, and from that day no one spoke out again.
claims.sourceText: 眾聞之遂帖然，自是不復有異言者。

claims.action: Huandu served four sovereigns across forty years. In battle he always met the enemy first; in great council his counsel was often followed.
claims.sourceText: 歡都事四君，出入四十年，征伐之際遇敵則先戰，廣廷大議多用其謀。

claims.action: Shizu once said: "With Huandu at my side, what could I not accomplish?"
claims.sourceText: 世祖嘗曰：「吾有歡都，則何事不成。」

claims.action: Under Suzong his trust outranked every courtier near the throne.
claims.sourceText: 肅宗時，委任冠於近僚。

claims.action: When Muzong came to the throne, every matter touching Liao was placed solely in his hands.
claims.sourceText: 穆宗嗣位，凡圖遼事皆專委之。

claims.action: Kangzong treated him as a veteran of his father and uncles' generation, honored him the more, and drew great profit from his service.
claims.sourceText: 康宗以為父叔舊人，尤加敬禮，多所補益。

claims.action: In the second month of Kangzong 11 (guisi) he fell ill, withdrew to the Milimei River to convalesce, and died at sixty-three.
claims.sourceText: 康宗十一年癸巳二月，得疾，避疾于米里每水，薨，年六十三。

claims.action: When the bier came home Kangzong met it on the road, escorted it to Huandu's house, and oversaw the burial himself.
claims.sourceText: 喪歸，康宗親迓于路，送至其家，親視葬事。

claims.action: In Tianhui 15 he was posthumously made Bearer of the Triple Staff with Equal Protocol and Duke of Dai.
claims.sourceText: 天會十五年，追贈儀同三司、代國公。

claims.action: In Mingchang 5 he was raised to Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Protocol and given the posthumous name Zhongmin, Loyal and Keen.
claims.sourceText: 明昌五年，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰忠敏。

claims.action: His sons were Gushen and Mouyan.
claims.sourceText: 子穀神、謀演。

claims.action: During Azu'a's revolt Mouyan went with Huandu and stood hostage in his place.
claims.sourceText: 謀演，當阿注阿之難，從歡都代為質。

claims.action: The tribal chiefs Laobolun, Baheru, and Xiabasu quarreled over a thousand-household command. The emperor said: "Have any of you served the state as Huandu and his son have?"
claims.sourceText: 孛堇老孛論、拔合汝、轄拔速三人爭千戶，上曰：「汝輩能如歡都父子有勞于國者乎。」

claims.action: Suzong had twice been beaten by Huanhan. Shizu sent Huandu and Yehe with the commandery levies of their tribes to reinforce him.
claims.sourceText: 肅宗拒桓赧已再失利，世祖命歡都、冶訶，以本部謀克之兵助之。

claims.action: Yehe and Huandu were always at Shizu's side, joining his councils in camp and taking their places in the battle line in the field. They were never absent from his affairs.
claims.sourceText: 冶訶與歡都常在世祖左右，居則與謀議，出則泣行陣，未嘗不在其間。

claims.action: In Mingchang 5 he was raised to Special Advancement with the posthumous name Zhongji, Loyal and Succoring, and together with Duke of Dai Huandu, Special Advancement Hezhe, Grand Master of the Palace Penna, and Bearer of the Triple Staff Bada was granted collateral sacrifice in Shizu's temple.
claims.sourceText: 明昌五年，贈特進，諡忠濟，與代國公歡都、特進劾者、開府儀同三司盆納、儀同三司拔達，俱配享世祖廟廷。

claims.action: The encomium reads: Virtuous Shilu was friend to Zhaozu; Huandu served Jingzu and Shizu as minister.
claims.sourceText: 贊曰：賢石魯與昭祖為友，歡都事景祖、世祖為之臣。

claims.action: From Jingzu's day Jin began its rise, and the lord-and-minister order among the tribes was first fixed. Hence among ministers of other surnames Huandu leads the roll.
claims.sourceText: 蓋金自景祖始大，諸部君臣之分始定，故傳異姓之臣，以歡都為首。

claims.action: He met the messenger on the road and reached home at noon. Azu'a told Muzong: "Let the noted bureaucrats of the registered Jurchen band together, send my brothers and kin by the Xianzhou road into Liao, give me gold from the treasury and horses from the stables without stint, and let Huandu escort me to the Liao frontier before he returns."
claims.sourceText: 中途逢告者，日午至，阿注阿謂穆宗曰：「可使系案女直知名官僚相結，送我兄弟親屬由咸州路入遼國，庫金廄馬與我勿惜，歡都亦當送我至遼境，然後還。」

claims.action: Yehe, though of the imperial house, shared Huandu's merit, and is therefore set down here beside him.
claims.sourceText: 冶訶雖宗室，與歡都同功，故列敘焉。

claims.sourceText: 與同部人把裏勃堇，斡泯水蒲察部胡都化勃堇、廝都勃堇，泰神忒保水完顏部安團勃堇，統門水溫蒂痕部活裏蓋勃堇，俱來歸，金之為國，自此益大。

claims.action: Gunan, Yehe's son, was skilled in horsemanship and archery and gifted with ability.

claims.action: Egunai, Yehe's son, was a man of imposing stature.
claims.sourceText: 訛古乃，冶訶子，姿質魁偉。

claims.action: In Mingchang 5 he was raised to Special Advancement with the posthumous name Zhongji, Loyal and Succoring, and together with Duke of Dai Huandu, Special Advancement Hezhe, Grand Master of the Palace Penna, and Bearer of the Triple Staff Bada was granted collateral sacrifice in Shizu's temple.
claims.sourceText: 明昌五年，贈特進，諡忠濟，與代國公歡都、特進劾者、開府儀同三司盆納、儀同三司拔達，俱配享世祖廟廷。

units.zh: 古者太史掌敘邦國之世次，辨其姓氏，別其昭穆，尚失。
units.en: Even in ancient times the Grand Historian who ordered the ages of the realms, sorted clan names, and marked senior from junior lines could not keep the record whole.
units.literal: In antiquity the Grand Historian kept the generations of the states, distinguished their surnames, and separated zhao from mu—and still there were lapses.

units.zh: 金人初起完毅十二部，其後皆以部為氏，史臣記錄有稱「宗室」者，有稱完顏者。
units.en: The Jin first gathered in the twelve Wanyi tribes, then took each tribe as a clan name. Court historians sometimes wrote "Imperial Clan", sometimes Wanyan.
units.literal: When the Jin people first arose in the twelve tribes of Wanyi, afterward all took their tribe as surname; in the historians' records some are called "Imperial Clan", some Wanyan.

units.zh: 稱完顏者亦有二焉，有同姓完顏，蓋疏族，若石土門、迪古乃是也；
units.en: "Wanyan" itself split two ways: same-surname Wanyan were really distant kin, men like Shitumen and Digunai;
units.literal: Those called Wanyan also fall into two kinds: same-surname Wanyan, who were in fact collateral kin—Shitumen and Digunai are examples;

units.zh: 有異姓完顏，蓋部人，若歡都是也。
units.en: different-surname Wanyan were really tribesmen, men like Huandu.
units.literal: and different-surname Wanyan, who were in fact men of the tribe—Huandu is an example.

units.zh: 大定以前稱「宗室」，明昌以後避睿宗諱稱「內族」，其實一而已，書名不書氏，其制如此。
units.en: Before Dading they were called "Imperial Clan"; after Mingchang, to avoid the taboo on Ruizong, "Inner Kin"—the same group in fact. Registers record personal names, not clan names; that was the rule.
units.literal: Before the Dading era they were called "Imperial Clan"; after Mingchang, to avoid the taboo on Ruizong they were called "Inner Kin"—in substance one and the same. The annals give personal names, not clan names; such was the rule.

units.zh: 宣宗詔宗室皆稱完顏，不復識別焉。
units.en: Emperor Xuanzong ordered that all imperial kin take the name Wanyan, and the old distinctions ceased.
units.literal: Emperor Xuanzong decreed that all of the imperial clan should be called Wanyan, and no further distinction was made.

units.zh: 大定、泰和之間，袒免以上親皆有屬籍，以敘授官，大功以上，薨卒輟朝，親親之道行焉。
units.en: From Dading through Taihe, relatives within tan-mian degree and nearer were entered in the clan rolls and ranked for appointment; when one within da-gong degree or nearer died, court paused in mourning—kinship was honored in deed.
units.literal: Between Dading and Taihe, kin within the degree of tan-mian mourning and closer all had household registers, by which offices were assigned; for kin within the degree of da-gong mourning and closer, death halted court audiences—the way of cherishing kin was practiced.

units.zh: 貞祐以後，譜牒散失，大概僅存，不可殫悉，今掇其可次第者著於篇。
units.en: After Zhenyou the pedigree books were lost; a broken outline alone remains, too fragmentary to exhaust. Here I collect what can still be sequenced and place it in these pages.
units.literal: After Zhenyou the genealogical registers were scattered and lost; only a rough outline survives, and it cannot be set forth in full. Now I gather what can be ordered by generation and set it down in this chapter.

units.zh: 其上無所系、下無所承者，不能盡錄也。
units.en: Lines that attach to nothing above and hand down to nothing below cannot be entered in full.
units.literal: Those with no tie above and no succession below cannot all be recorded.

units.literal: The imperial granduncle, Grand Preceptor, as a brother fulfilled all fraternal love and toward the state harbored only loyalty; every plan was without error, and nothing he undertook failed.

units.zh: 愛民長悌曰'恭'，一德不懈曰'簡'，夙夜共事 曰'敬'，小心畏忌曰'僖'，請上皇伯祖太師尊諡曰恭簡皇帝，廟號康宗、妣曰敬僖皇后。
units.en: Gong is for loving the people and long practicing fraternal duty, jian for single-minded virtue without slackening, jing for toiling from dawn to dusk in service, xi for cautious reverence and restraint—we ask that the imperial granduncle, Grand Preceptor, receive the posthumous title Emperor Gongjian, with the temple name Kangzong, and that his consort be titled Empress Jingxi.
units.literal: Gong is for loving the people and long practicing fraternal duty, jian for single-minded virtue without slackening, jing for toiling from dawn to dusk in service, xi for cautious reverence and restraint—we request the posthumous honorific title Emperor Gongjian for the imperial granduncle, Grand Preceptor, with the temple name Kangzong, and Empress Jingxi for his consort.

units.zh: 是歲閏十一月，增上祖宗尊諡，始祖景元皇帝曰懿憲景元皇帝，德皇帝曰淵穆玄德皇帝，安皇帝曰和靖慶安皇帝，獻祖定昭皇帝曰純烈定昭皇帝，昭祖成襄皇帝曰武惠成襄皇帝，景祖惠桓皇帝曰英烈惠桓皇帝，世祖聖肅皇帝曰神武聖肅皇帝，肅宗穆憲皇帝曰明睿穆憲皇帝，穆宗孝平皇帝曰章順孝平皇帝，康宗恭簡皇帝曰獻敏恭簡皇帝，太宗文烈皇帝曰體元應運世德昭功哲惠仁聖文烈皇帝，徽宗景宣皇帝曰允恭克讓孝德玄功佑聖景宣皇帝，已上廟號如故。
units.en: In the intercalary eleventh month of that year the court augmented the posthumous titles of the imperial ancestors: Founder Emperor Jingyuan became Emperor Yixian Jingyuan; Emperor De became Emperor Yuanmu Xuande; Emperor An became Emperor Hejing Qing'an; Xianzu Emperor Dingzhao became Emperor Chunlie Dingzhao; Zhaozu Emperor Chengxiang became Emperor Wuhui Chengxiang; Jingzu Emperor Huihuan became Emperor Yinglie Huihuan; Shizu Emperor Shengsu became Emperor Shenwu Shengsu; Suzong Emperor Muxian became Emperor Mingrui Muxian; Muzong Emperor Xiaoping became Emperor Zhangshun Xiaoping; Kangzong Emperor Gongjian became Emperor Xianmin Gongjian; Taizong Emperor Wenlie became Emperor Tiyuan Yingyun Shide Zhaogong Zhehui Rensheng Wenlie; Huizong Emperor Jingxuan became Emperor Yungong Kerang Xiaode Xuangong Yousheng Jingxuan—the temple names listed above remained unchanged.
units.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month of that year, augmented honorific titles were conferred upon the imperial ancestors: the Founder Emperor Jingyuan became Emperor Yixian Jingyuan; Emperor De became Emperor Yuanmu Xuande; Emperor An became Emperor Hejing Qing'an; Xianzu Emperor Dingzhao became Emperor Chunlie Dingzhao; Zhaozu Emperor Chengxiang became Emperor Wuhui Chengxiang; Jingzu Emperor Huihuan became Emperor Yinglie Huihuan; Shizu Emperor Shengsu became Emperor Shenwu Shengsu; Suzong Emperor Muxian became Emperor Mingrui Muxian; Muzong Emperor Xiaoping became Emperor Zhangshun Xiaoping; Kangzong Emperor Gongjian became Emperor Xianmin Gongjian; Taizong Emperor Wenlie became Emperor Tiyuan Yingyun Shide Zhaogong Zhehui Rensheng Wenlie; Huizong Emperor Jingxuan became Emperor Yungong Kerang Xiaode Xuangong Yousheng Jingxuan—the temple names above remained as before.

units.zh: 丙辰，奉上九代祖妣尊諡廟號，是日百僚上表稱賀。
units.en: On the bingchen day the court presented posthumous titles and temple names for the nine generations of ancestors and consorts; that same day the officials submitted memorials of congratulation.
units.literal: On the bingchen day, posthumous honorific titles and temple names for the nine generations of imperial ancestors and consorts were presented; on that day the hundred officials submitted memorials of congratulation.

units.en: Huandu was of the Wanyan tribe.
units.literal: Huandu was a man of the Wanyan tribe.

units.zh: 明昌五年，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰忠敏。
units.en: In Mingchang 5 he was raised to Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Protocol and given the posthumous name Zhongmin, Loyal and Keen.
units.literal: In Mingchang year 5 he was further enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Protocol and given the posthumous title Zhongmin, "Loyal and Keen."

units.en: His sons were Gushen and Mouyan.
units.literal: His sons were Gushen and Mouyan.

units.zh: 穆宗德歡都言，後以撻懶女曷羅哂妻其子谷神。
units.en: Muzong remembered Huandu's counsel and later arranged for Talan's daughter Heluoshen to marry Huandu's son Gushen.
units.literal: Muzong was grateful for Huandu's words; later he gave Talan's daughter Heluoshen in marriage to Huandu's son Gushen.

units.en: When Shizu first came to power, Huandu inherited the post of military governor.
units.literal: At the beginning of Shizu's reign he inherited the office of military governor.

units.zh: 遼人命穆宗、太祖、辭不失、歡都俱為詳穩。
units.en: Liao appointed Muzong, Taizu, Cibushi, and Huandu each to the office of xiangwen.
units.literal: The Liao appointed Muzong, Taizu, Cibushi, and Huandu all as xiangwen.

units.zh: 歡都為都統，往治斜缽失軍之狀，盡解斜缽所將軍、大破烏春、窩謀罕於斜堆，擒故石、拔石。
units.en: Huandu was made commander-in-chief and sent to investigate Xiebo's loss of the force. He relieved Xiebo of his entire command, crushed Wuchun and Womouhan at Xiedui, and captured Gushi and Bashi.
units.literal: Huandu served as commander-in-chief, investigated the circumstances of Xiebo's loss of the force, removed all the troops from Xiebo's command, routed Wuchun and Womouhan at Xiedui, and captured Gushi and Bashi.

units.zh: 天會十五年，追贈儀同三司、代國公。
units.en: In Tianhui 15 he was posthumously made Bearer of the Triple Staff with Equal Protocol and Duke of Dai.
units.literal: In Tianhui year 15 he was posthumously enfeoffed as Bearer of the Triple Staff with Equal Protocol and Duke of Dai.

units.zh: 歡都事四君，出入四十年，征伐之際遇敵則先戰，廣廷大議多用其謀。
units.en: Huandu served four sovereigns across forty years. In battle he always met the enemy first; in great council his counsel was often followed.
units.literal: Huandu served four rulers, coming and going for forty years; on campaigns when he met the enemy he fought first; in broad court deliberations his counsel was often used.

units.zh: 康宗十一年癸巳二月，得疾，避疾于米里每水，薨，年六十三。
units.en: In the second month of Kangzong 11 (guisi) he fell ill, withdrew to the Milimei River to convalesce, and died at sixty-three.
units.literal: In the second month of Kangzong year 11, guisi, he fell ill, withdrew to the Milimei River to avoid illness, and died at age sixty-three.

units.zh: 歡都被甲執戟而起曰：「彼為亂之人也，若取太師兄弟，則亦與之乎。
units.en: Huandu buckled on armor, seized his halberd, and rose. "He is a rebel. If they demand the Grand Preceptor's brothers, will you surrender them as well?
units.literal: Huandu donned armor, took up his halberd, and rose, saying: "He is a man of disorder. If they take the Grand Preceptor's brothers, will you hand them over too?

units.zh: 今取我輩，我輩決不可往，若必用戰，當盡力致死。」
units.en: If they demand us, we will never go. If it must come to war, we shall fight to the last man."
units.literal: If they take us now, we absolutely will not go. If battle is necessary, we shall fight to the death."

units.zh: 歡都下馬執轡而諫曰：「獨不念愛弟蒲陽溫與弟婦乎。」
units.en: Huandu dismounted, seized the bridle, and pleaded: "Have you no thought for your beloved younger brother Puyangwen and his wife?"
units.literal: Huandu dismounted, took the reins, and remonstrated: "Will you not think of your beloved younger brother Puyangwen and your younger brother's wife?"

units.zh: 歡都入見阿注阿曰：「汝輩所謀之事奈何。
units.en: Huandu went in to Azu'a and said: "What end do you intend for this plot of yours?
units.literal: Huandu went in to see Azu'a and said: "What is to become of the affair you are plotting?

units.zh: 閨門眷屬豈足劫質，徒使之驚恐耳。
units.en: The women of the inner quarters are poor hostages; you only terrify them to no purpose.
units.literal: Women and kin of the inner quarters are hardly fit hostages—they only frighten them for nothing.

units.zh: 汝固識我，盍以我為質也。」
units.en: You know me well. Take me instead."
units.literal: You know me well—why not take me as hostage instead?"

units.zh: 歡都曰：「汝輩若紛爭，則吾必不默默但已。」
units.en: Huandu said: "If you quarrel among yourselves, I shall not stand idly by."
units.literal: Huandu said: "If you contend among yourselves, I shall certainly not remain silent."

units.zh: 祖石魯，與昭祖同時同部同名，交相得，誓曰：「生則同川居，死則同穀葬。」
units.en: His grandfather Shilu was Zhaozu's contemporary, clansman, and namesake; the two became fast friends and swore an oath: "In life we shall share one river's bank; in death one valley's grave."
units.literal: His grandfather Shilu lived in the same age, the same tribe, and bore the same name as Zhaozu; they took a liking to each other and swore: "While we live we shall dwell on the same river; when we die we shall be buried in the same valley."

units.zh: 土人呼昭祖為勇石魯，呼石魯為賢石魯。
units.en: The people called Zhaozu "Brave Shilu" and Shilu "Virtuous Shilu."
units.literal: The people called Zhaozu "Brave Shilu" and called Shilu "Virtuous Shilu."

units.zh: 昭祖與石魯謀取之，遂偕至嶺右，炷火於箭端而射。
units.en: Zhaozu and Shilu plotted to recover them, went together beyond the ridge, and shot arrows tipped with burning tinder.
units.literal: Zhaozu and Shilu plotted to take them, went together to the right of the ridge, lit fire on the arrowheads, and shot.

units.zh: 昭祖及石魯以眾至，攻取其貲產，虜二女子以歸。
units.en: Zhaozu and Shilu then marched in force, seized their goods, and carried off the two women.
units.literal: Zhaozu and Shilu came with their forces, seized their goods, and carried off the two women.

units.zh: 昭祖納其一，賢石魯納其一，皆以為妾。
units.en: Zhaozu took one for himself and Virtuous Shilu the other; each made his a concubine.
units.literal: Zhaozu took one and Virtuous Shilu the other, each as concubine.

units.zh: 是時，諸部不肯用條教，昭祖耀武於青嶺、白山，入于蘇濱、耶懶之地，賢石魯佐之也。
units.en: The tribes still refused law and custom. Zhaozu showed his strength at Qingling and White Mountain and pressed into Subin and Yelan, with Virtuous Shilu at his side throughout.
units.literal: At that time the tribes would not accept regulations; Zhaozu displayed martial prowess at Qingling and White Mountain and entered the lands of Subin and Yelan, and Virtuous Shilu assisted him.

units.zh: 至景祖時，石魯之子劾孫舉部來歸，居於安出虎水源胡凱山南。
units.en: In Jingzu's day Shilu's son Hesun brought his tribe in submission and settled south of Hukai Mountain on the headwaters of the Anchu River.
units.literal: In the time of Jingzu, Shilu's son Hesun brought his whole tribe to submit and dwelt south of Hukai Mountain on the Anchu River.

units.zh: 歡都入與謀議，出臨戰陣，未嘗去左右。
units.en: Huandu came in to counsel and went out to command on the field; he never left Shizu's side.
units.literal: Huandu went in to counsel on plans and went out to face the battle lines, never leaving Shizu's side.

units.zh: 斡勒部人杯乃，自景祖時與其兄弟俱居安出虎水之北，及烏春作難，杯乃將與烏春合，間誘斡魯紺出水居人與之相結，欲先除去歡都。
units.en: Beinai of the Wole clan had lived with his brothers north of the Anchu River since Jingzu's day. When Wuchun rebelled, Beinai was ready to join him and secretly won over the Woluguan water-folk, intending to destroy Huandu first.
units.literal: Beinai of the Wole tribe, since Jingzu's time he and his brothers had all dwelt north of the Anchu River; when Wuchun made trouble, Beinai was about to join Wuchun and between whiles enticed the water-dwellers of Woluguan to link with him, wishing first to remove Huandu.

units.zh: 會其家被火，陰約隸人不歌束，詭稱放火乃歡都、胡土二人，使注都來謂世祖曰：「不歌束來告曰'前日之火，歡都等縱之'。
units.en: When his house burned, he secretly suborned the bondservant Bugesou to claim that Huandu and Hutu had set the blaze, and sent Zhudu to Shizu with the message: "Bugesou reports that the fire the other day was the work of Huandu and his party.
units.literal: When his house caught fire, he secretly arranged with the bondservant Bugesou, falsely claiming the arsonists were Huandu and Hutu, and sent Zhudu to tell Shizu: "Bugesou comes to report that the fire of the other day was set by Huandu and the rest.

units.zh: 穆宗曰：「壯哉歡都，以我所見，正如此爾。」
units.en: Muzong said: "How bold Huandu is! In my judgment he is entirely right."
units.literal: Muzong said: "How stalwart is Huandu! From what I see, it is exactly so."

units.zh: 贈歡都以馬，曰：「戰則乘此。」
units.en: He gave Huandu a horse and said: "When you fight, ride this one."
units.literal: He gifted Huandu a horse, saying: "In battle ride this."

units.zh: 世祖乃往見杯乃，隔鱉刺水而與之言曰：「不歌束既告縱火由歡都等，謹當如約。
units.en: Shizu then went to Beinai and, standing across the Biecih River, said: "Bugesou has named Huandu and the rest as the arsonists. I shall keep our agreement to the letter.
units.literal: Shizu then went to see Beinai, and across the Biecih River spoke to him: "Since Bugesou has reported that the arson was by Huandu and the others, I shall strictly keep the agreement.

units.zh: 既而聞之，放火者杯乃家人阿出胡山也，杯乃欲開此釁，故以誣歡都雲。
units.en: It later came out that the fire had been set by Beinai's servant Achuhushan. Beinai had sought a pretext for strife and had framed Huandu.
units.literal: Later it was learned that the one who set the fire was Beinai's household servant Achuhushan; Beinai wished to open this quarrel and therefore falsely accused Huandu.

units.zh: 日已曛，惟從五六十騎，歡都入敵陣鏖擊之，左右出入者數四，世祖中創乃止。
units.en: Dusk had fallen and Shizu had barely fifty or sixty riders. Huandu plunged into the enemy line and fought back and forth four times over before Shizu, wounded, called a halt.
units.literal: The sun had set; Shizu had only fifty or sixty horsemen with him; Huandu charged into the enemy ranks and fought fiercely, going in and out several times; Shizu was wounded and only then did they stop.

units.zh: 於是騷臘勃堇、富者撻懶歡勝負不助軍，而騷臘、撻懶先曾與臘醅、麻產合，世祖欲因軍還而遂滅之，馳馬前進。
units.en: The tribal chiefs Saola and Fuzhe Talan watched to see which side would win and withheld their support. Both had previously joined Lapei and Machan, so Shizu meant to destroy them on the march home and spurred his horse forward.
units.literal: Thereupon the tribal chiefs Saola and Fuzhe Talan watched the outcome and did not aid the army. Saola and Talan had earlier joined with Lapei and Machan, so Shizu wished to destroy them on the army's return and spurred his horse forward.

units.zh: 撻懶者，貞惠皇后之弟也。
units.en: Talan was Empress Zhenhui's younger brother.
units.literal: Talan was the younger brother of Empress Zhenhui.

units.en: Shizu was moved and drew rein.
units.literal: Shizu was moved by his words and stopped.

units.zh: 蒲陽溫者，漢語雲幼弟也。
units.en: Puyangwen is the Jurchen name for "younger brother" in Chinese.

units.zh: 世祖母弟中穆宗最少，故雲然。
units.en: Of Shizu's maternal brothers Muzong was the youngest, and so earned that name.
units.literal: Among Shizu's maternal younger brothers Muzong was the youngest, and therefore he was so called.

units.zh: 太祖追麻產，歡都射中其首，遂獲之。
units.en: When Taizu pursued Machan, Huandu struck him in the head with an arrow and took him prisoner.
units.literal: Taizu pursued Machan; Huandu shot him in the head and he was captured.

units.zh: 斡善、斡脫以姑裏甸兵來歸，使斜缽勃堇撫定之。
units.en: Woshan and Wotuo brought the Guli contingent in submission, and Shizu sent the tribal chief Xiebo to settle them.
units.literal: Woshan and Wotuo brought the Guli troops to submit; Shizu sent the tribal chief Xiebo to pacify and settle them.

units.zh: 蒲察部故石、拔石等，誘其眾入城，陷三百餘人。
units.en: Gushi, Bashi, and others of the Pucha tribe lured the troops into a city and trapped more than three hundred men.
units.literal: Gushi, Bashi, and others of the Pucha tribe enticed their forces into the city and trapped more than three hundred men.

units.zh: 辭不失破烏春窩謀罕城，獲三濱、撒達，並獲其母，以為次室，撫其二子。
units.en: When Cibushi stormed the stronghold of Wuchun and Womouhan he took Sanbin and Sada and their mother as well. He made her a secondary consort and raised the two boys.
units.literal: Cibushi captured the city of Wuchun and Womouhan, took Sanbin and Sada, and also took their mother, making her a secondary wife and nurturing the two sons.

units.zh: 因穆宗晨出獵，糾率七八人操兵入宅，奪據寢門，劫貞惠皇后及家人等。
units.en: While Muzong was out hunting at dawn, he rallied seven or eight armed men, forced their way into the palace, seized the inner gate, and took Empress Zhenhui and the household hostage.
units.literal: Taking advantage of Muzong's morning hunt, he gathered seven or eight men with weapons, entered the residence, seized the sleeping quarters' gate, and held Empress Zhenhui and the household hostage.

units.zh: 再三言之，阿注阿從之，貞惠皇后乃得解，而質歡都。
units.en: He pressed the point again and again until Azu'a agreed. The empress was freed and Huandu held in her place.
units.literal: He spoke thus again and again; Azu'a consented; Empress Zhenhui was released, and Huandu was held hostage.

units.zh: 遂執歡都及阿魯太彎、阿魯不太彎等七人，以衣裾相結，與阿注阿俱行，至遼境，乃釋歡都。
units.en: They bound Huandu together with Alutaiwan, Alutaibuwan, and five others, linking their robe-hems, and marched with Azu'a. At the Liao border they set Huandu free.
units.literal: They then seized Huandu and Alutaiwan, Alutaibuwan, and six others, tied their garment skirts together, and marched with Azu'a; when they reached Liao territory they released Huandu.

units.zh: 歡都至濟州，實黃龍府，使人馳驛要遮阿注阿黨屬，惟縱其親人使去。
units.en: Huandu reached Jizhou, which was in fact Huanglong Prefecture, and sent riders by relay to cut off Azu'a's party, sparing only his kin.
units.literal: Huandu reached Jizhou—in fact Huanglong Prefecture—and sent men by relay post to intercept Azu'a's followers, releasing only his kin to go.

units.zh: 遂殺三濱並其母，具報於遼，乞還阿注阿，遼人流之曷堇城。
units.en: He then killed Sanbin and his mother, reported the whole affair to Liao, and asked that Azu'a be returned. Liao banished him to Yijin.
units.literal: He then killed Sanbin and his mother, reported fully to Liao, and begged the return of Azu'a; Liao exiled him to Yijin city.

units.zh: 其後，阿注阿懷思鄉土，亡歸，附於系案女直，因亂其官僚之室，捕之，不伏，乃見殺。
units.en: Later, homesick for his own country, Azu'a fled back and joined the registered Jurchen. He raided the dwellings of their officials, was seized, refused to yield, and was executed.
units.literal: Later Azu'a longed for his native land, fled back, attached himself to the registered Jurchen, and by disturbing the chambers of their bureaucrats was captured; he would not submit and was put to death.

units.zh: 穆宗襲位之初，諸父之子習烈、斜缽及諸兄有異言，曰：「君相之位，皆渠輩為之，奈何？」
units.en: Early in Muzong's reign, his cousins Xilie and Xiebo, together with his elder brothers, murmured dissent: "Those men made themselves lord and minister—what of us?"
units.literal: At the beginning of Muzong's succession, his cousins Xilie and Xiebo, sons of his father's brothers, and his elder brothers had dissenting words, saying: "The positions of lord and minister were all made by them—what then?"

units.zh: 眾聞之遂帖然，自是不復有異言者。
units.en: At his words the company fell quiet, and from that day no one spoke out again.
units.literal: When the multitude heard this they became submissive, and from then on there were no more dissenting words.

units.zh: 世祖嘗曰：「吾有歡都，則何事不成。」
units.en: Shizu once said: "With Huandu at my side, what could I not accomplish?"
units.literal: Shizu once said: "With Huandu at my side, what affair could fail?"

units.en: Under Suzong his trust outranked every courtier near the throne.
units.literal: Under Suzong his commission ranked above the close attendants.

units.zh: 穆宗嗣位，凡圖遼事皆專委之。
units.en: When Muzong came to the throne, every matter touching Liao was placed solely in his hands.
units.literal: When Muzong succeeded, all affairs concerning Liao were entrusted to him alone.

units.zh: 康宗以為父叔舊人，尤加敬禮，多所補益。
units.en: Kangzong treated him as a veteran of his father and uncles' generation, honored him the more, and drew great profit from his service.
units.literal: Kangzong regarded him as an old companion of his father and uncles and showed him especial respect and courtesy, benefiting greatly from him.

units.zh: 喪歸，康宗親迓于路，送至其家，親視葬事。
units.en: When the bier came home Kangzong met it on the road, escorted it to Huandu's house, and oversaw the burial himself.
units.literal: When the funeral procession returned, Kangzong personally met it on the road, escorted it to his home, and personally oversaw the burial.

units.zh: 謀演，當阿注阿之難，從歡都代為質。
units.en: During Azu'a's revolt Mouyan went with Huandu and stood hostage in his place.
units.literal: Mouyan, during Azu'a's crisis, followed Huandu and served as hostage in his stead.

units.zh: 孛堇老孛論、拔合汝、轄拔速三人爭千戶，上曰：「汝輩能如歡都父子有勞于國者乎。」
units.en: The tribal chiefs Laobolun, Baheru, and Xiabasu quarreled over a thousand-household command. The emperor said: "Have any of you served the state as Huandu and his son have?"
units.literal: The tribal chiefs Laobolun, Baheru, and Xiabasu disputed over command of a thousand households; the emperor said: "Can you be like Huandu and his son, who have labored for the state?"

units.zh: 肅宗拒桓赧已再失利，世祖命歡都、冶訶，以本部謀克之兵助之。
units.en: Suzong had twice been beaten by Huanhan. Shizu sent Huandu and Yehe with the commandery levies of their tribes to reinforce him.
units.literal: Suzong in resisting Huanhan had already suffered defeat twice; Shizu ordered Huandu and Yehe to assist him with the commandery troops of their own tribes.

units.zh: 冶訶與歡都常在世祖左右，居則與謀議，出則泣行陣，未嘗不在其間。
units.en: Yehe and Huandu were always at Shizu's side, joining his councils in camp and taking their places in the battle line in the field. They were never absent from his affairs.
units.literal: Yehe and Huandu were constantly at Shizu's side; at home they joined his deliberations, and in the field they took their places in the battle line, never absent from his affairs.

units.zh: 明昌五年，贈特進，諡忠濟，與代國公歡都、特進劾者、開府儀同三司盆納、儀同三司拔達，俱配享世祖廟廷。
units.en: In Mingchang 5 he was raised to Special Advancement with the posthumous name Zhongji, Loyal and Succoring, and together with Duke of Dai Huandu, Special Advancement Hezhe, Grand Master of the Palace Penna, and Bearer of the Triple Staff Bada was granted collateral sacrifice in Shizu's temple.
units.literal: In Mingchang year 5 he was further enfeoffed as Special Advancement with the posthumous title Zhongji, "Loyal and Succoring," and together with Duke of Dai Huandu, Special Advancement Hezhe, Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Protocol Penna, and Bearer of the Triple Staff with Equal Protocol Bada, all received collateral sacrifice in Shizu's temple hall.

units.zh: 贊曰：賢石魯與昭祖為友，歡都事景祖、世祖為之臣。
units.en: The encomium reads: Virtuous Shilu was friend to Zhaozu; Huandu served Jingzu and Shizu as minister.
units.literal: The encomium says: Virtuous Shilu was Zhaozu's friend; Huandu served Jingzu and Shizu as their minister.

units.zh: 蓋金自景祖始大，諸部君臣之分始定，故傳異姓之臣，以歡都為首。
units.en: From Jingzu's day Jin began its rise, and the lord-and-minister order among the tribes was first fixed. Hence among ministers of other surnames Huandu leads the roll.
units.literal: Jin from Jingzu's time began to grow great, and the distinction between lord and minister among the tribes was first fixed; therefore in biographies of ministers of other surnames, Huandu stands first.

units.zh: 中途逢告者，日午至，阿注阿謂穆宗曰：「可使系案女直知名官僚相結，送我兄弟親屬由咸州路入遼國，庫金廄馬與我勿惜，歡都亦當送我至遼境，然後還。」
units.en: He met the messenger on the road and reached home at noon. Azu'a told Muzong: "Let the noted bureaucrats of the registered Jurchen band together, send my brothers and kin by the Xianzhou road into Liao, give me gold from the treasury and horses from the stables without stint, and let Huandu escort me to the Liao frontier before he returns."
units.literal: Midway he met the messenger; by noon he arrived. Azu'a said to Muzong: "You may have the well-known bureaucrats of the registered Jurchen join together, send my brothers and kin by the Xianzhou route into Liao territory, give me storehouses of gold and stables of horses without stint, and Huandu must also escort me to the Liao border and then return."

units.zh: 冶訶雖宗室，與歡都同功，故列敘焉。
units.en: Yehe, though of the imperial house, shared Huandu's merit, and is therefore set down here beside him.
units.literal: Yehe, though of the imperial clan, shared merit with Huandu; therefore he is narrated here as well.

units.zh: 列傳第六 ○歡都子 謀演 冶訶子 阿魯補 骨赧 訛古乃 蒲查
units.en: Biographies 6: Huandu and his son Mouyan; Yehe and his sons Alubu, Gunan, and Egunai; Sanda's son Pucha
units.literal: Biographies 6: Huandu and his son Mouyan; Yehe and his sons Alubu, Gunan, and Egunai; Sanda's son Pucha

units.zh: 骨赧，冶訶子，善騎射，有材幹。
units.en: Gunan, Yehe's son, was skilled in horsemanship and archery and gifted with ability.
units.literal: Gunan was Yehe's son, skilled in horsemanship and archery, and possessed of ability.

units.zh: 訛古乃，冶訶子，姿質魁偉。
units.en: Egunai, Yehe's son, was a man of imposing stature.
units.literal: Egunai was Yehe's son, imposing in stature and bearing.

units.zh: 冶訶子阿魯補、骨赧、訛古乃、散荅。
units.en: Yehe's sons were Alubu, Gunan, Egunai, and Sanda.
units.literal: Yehe's sons were Alubu, Gunan, Egunai, and Sanda.

units.zh: 複從其兄虞劃，率兵三千攻乾州，虞劃道病卒，代領其眾，至乾州，降其軍及營帳三十，獲印四十，與僕虺攻下義州。
units.en: He again followed his elder brother Yuhua with three thousand men against Qianzhou. Yuhua died on the march and Alubu took over his command. At Qianzhou he received the surrender of the garrison and thirty encampments, seized forty seals, and with Puhui reduced Yizhou.
units.literal: He again followed his elder brother Yuhua, leading three thousand men to attack Qianzhou; Yuhua died of illness on the road; Alubu took command of his force; reaching Qianzhou he received the surrender of their army and thirty encampments, seized forty seals, and with Puhui captured Yizhou.

units.zh: 冶訶系出景祖，居神隱水完顏部，為其部勃堇。
units.en: Yehe traced his line to Jingzu, lived with the Wanyan on the Shenyin River, and was chief of his division.
units.literal: Yehe was descended from Jingzu, dwelt with the Wanyan tribe on the Shenyin River, and was tribal chief of his division.

units.zh: 天會十五年，贈銀青光祿大夫。
units.en: In Tianhui 15 he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver-Green Tally.
units.literal: In Tianhui year 15 he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver-Green Tally.

units.zh: 與同部人把裏勃堇，斡泯水蒲察部胡都化勃堇、廝都勃堇，泰神忒保水完顏部安團勃堇，統門水溫蒂痕部活裏蓋勃堇，俱來歸，金之為國，自此益大。
units.en: Yehe came in submission together with Balai of his own division, Huduhua and Sidu of the Pucha on the Womin River, Antuan of the Wanyan on the Taishentebai River, and Huoligai of the Wendihen on the Tongmen River. From that time the Jin state grew still stronger.
units.literal: Together with Balai, tribal chief of the same division, Huduhua and Sidu, tribal chiefs of the Pucha tribe on the Womin River, Antuan, tribal chief of the Wanyan tribe on the Taishentebai River, and Huoligai, tribal chief of the Wendihen tribe on the Tongmen River, they all came to submit; from this the Jin state grew ever greater.

units.zh: 太祖崩，帝與兄宗幹率宗室群臣立太宗。
units.en: When Taizu died, the emperor with his elder brother Zonggan led the imperial clan and ministers to install Taizong.
units.literal: When Taizu died, the emperor with his elder brother Zonggan led the imperial clan and ministers to install Taizong.

units.zh: 以八月往陝西，或使宗弼遂將以行，或宗輔、宗幹、希尹中以一人往。」
units.en: In the eighth month march on Shaanxi—either Zongbi leads the whole way, or one of Zongfu, Zonggan, and Xiyin goes."
units.literal: In the eighth month go to Shaanxi—either have Zongbi lead the army through, or send one among Zongfu, Zonggan, and Xiyin."
